Please research this question using your tools. You MUST conclude your final response with exactly one of the following lines: 'FINAL DECISION: YES', 'FINAL DECISION: NO', or 'FINAL DECISION: MAYBE'.

Report study details, direction of effects, experimental mechanism/interventions, and PMID or citation; distinguish exact evidence from related studies.'}

The exact primary-literature match is **“CXCL13 inhibits microRNA-23a through PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in adipose tissue derived-mesenchymal stem cells”** (PMID **27509223**; *Biomedicine & Pharmacotherapy*, 2016). The paper uses **CXCL13**; the search did not establish “cXCL13” as a distinct factor. [Search results](call_2YeneUkBEfXQSm5mKEY9qA6M; call_Zk2lkzrC2onedE0amCfriGsb)

The study treated adipose tissue-derived MSCs isolated from healthy subjects (termed AMSCs) with CXCL13. It reports **decreased miR-23a** and **increased Runx2**, measured by real-time PCR and Western blot. A PI3K/AKT-specific inhibitor reversed both effects, while SAPK/JNK and ERK1/2 inhibitors did not—supporting PI3K/AKT involvement in these cells. [Abstract and study details](call_l5psMLtOPxj4vLzdR06HxY91)

**Evidence limits:** The accessible record does not give inhibitor identity, dose, treatment timing, sample size, or full-text mechanistic detail. PubTator annotations likewise tag CXCL13–MIR23A as a negative correlation, but are annotations of the same paper, not an independent replication. No distinct “cXCL13” study or separate corroborating primary study was identified. [Annotations](call_5d6DxOqs2zTwK2ZzijXsvJKi)
